clue.text: Source of report that won't harm anyone

definitions.text: Source of report that won't harm anyone

parts.words: Source of report that won't harm anyone
parts.note: a report is a loud bang, here from a gun loaded with a charge but no bullet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' suggests a document from a harmless source, but it is the noise of a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge holding powder without a bullet makes the bang of a shot while firing nothing that can wound.

clue.text: Expert on cause of ill-feeling — dreadful blog atrocities

indicators.note: dreadful suggests these letters are in a terrible mess, to be put right

explanation.surface: A scientist resents some dreadful posts online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but here it means feeling ill: germs cause sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria cause many diseases, and a scientist who studies them is a specialist in germs.

clue.text: Surrounding doctor that is protected by soldier, perhaps

indicators.note: the doctor and that-is letters sit within the insect, which shields them

parts.note: a soldier is one kind of ant, so ant is the example
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A medic under military guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the environment all around, as in ambient temperature or noise.

clue.text: Royalty on paperback for resident of Falklands

parts.note: a king is royalty
Penguin is the famous publisher of paperback books, so a paperback may be a Penguin

explanation.surface: A monarch is reading a cheap book on a South Atlantic island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Falkland Islands host large colonies of this big penguin species.

clue.text: Starts off in car at very important part of road system

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, which the instruction says to remove from each of the words
off means taken away, so each word loses its opening letter
in tells us where the removal happens: within the following three words

explanation.surface: Setting off in a car along a main route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off in car at very' is one instruction: drop the first letter of each of the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road is called an artery, a metaphor from the major blood vessels.

clue.text: Cutting troops, initially, on border with China

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter

parts.note: first letter of troops
a rim is an edge or border
Ming was a Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Cuts to army numbers on the Chinese frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimming is clipping, the act of cutting away small amounts, as with a hedge or hair.

clue.text: Conditions created by followers of her letters

wordplay.reading: the letters after H, E and R

parts.note: in the alphabet, I follows H, F follows E and S follows R

explanation.surface: Requirements set out by her correspondents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Followers of her letters' suggests her fans or pen friends; it means the letters coming after H, E, R in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are conditions or provisos, as in no ifs or buts.

clue.text: Part in theatre with purpose, unexpected good fortune

parts.note: the gods are the highest gallery in a theatre
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An actor landing a meaningful role has a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests an acting role, but it is a part of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is a welcome blessing that arrives unexpectedly, as though sent from heaven.

clue.text: Kind of analyst who won't give one treatment?

definitions.text: Kind of analyst who won't give one treatment?

parts.words: Kind of analyst who won't give one treatment?
parts.note: 'one' is read as a single person: this therapist treats people only together, never alone

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like an analyst refusing to treat you; in fact the treatment is only ever given to several at once.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of therapist runs sessions in which several patients are treated together.

clue.text: Furniture that's assembled in Number Ten

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cupboard with shelves or drawers
second meaning: the senior ministers who meet at 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembled' hints at flat-pack furniture, but it means gathered together for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a storage cupboard and the body of senior government ministers who meet at Downing Street.

clue.text: Someone who knows more than most how apples may be used, we hear

definitions.text: Someone who knows more than most

indicators.note: says the phrase is to be taken by its sound, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: apples go into cider, so they are used 'in cider'

explanation.surface: A know-all explaining what apples are good for.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on the inside of an organisation has privileged information unavailable to outsiders.

clue.text: Watch in middle of storm

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look at, observe (a verb)
second meaning: the calm centre of a hurricane

explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' looks like an instruction to take the central letter of 'storm', but it is a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep an eye on something is to observe it, and the calm centre of a cyclone is called its eye.

clue.text: Top amateur excited about new piece of luggage

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, or about, the single letter
excited words are stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A first-rate amateur gets worked up over a new bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling case opening into two halves, an old-fashioned kind of suitcase.

clue.text: Raft I anchor at sea in area south of Malta

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A raft drops anchor in the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya and Tunisia lie across the sea due south of Malta, on the northern coast of the continent.

clue.text: Design setting for ring

definitions.meaning: first meaning: purpose or aim (a noun)
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting for ring' suggests jewellery, but the ring is a circus ring, found 'in tent'.
explanation.definitionFit: One's purpose or aim is one's intention, a meaning shared by design as a noun.

clue.text: Place in Devon, moving on West, as yet unsettled

indicators.note: the two letters 'on' are moved to the left, westward, the front of the word

parts.note: Crediton is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone relocating from a Devon town westward hasn't yet settled in.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought on credit are taken now with the bill left unpaid, so the account is not yet settled.

clue.text: Quartet of players and person of 13 turning up in TV studio

parts.note: the four bridge players are North, East, West and South

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: 13 down is North Africa, and a Moor is a person from there

explanation.surface: Four performers and a North African come up to a television studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsroom is where news is gathered and presented, as in a broadcaster's studio.

clue.text: Tempted sailor inside with love — not easily done

indicators.note: the sailor and love are placed within the word for tempted

parts.note: lured means tempted or enticed
AB is an able-bodied seaman
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone seduced a sailor and fell in love, a tale with something awkward about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is laboured has been achieved only with great effort and strain.

clue.text: Scholars giving bishop sign about authorisation

indicators.note: the word for sign goes about, around, the authorisation

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come
an OK is approval or authorisation

explanation.surface: Academics give a bishop a signal about permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmen are literary or learned people, lovers of books.

clue.text: After one gets inside, drive away carriage

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the word for drive away

parts.note: to chase off is to drive away
Roman numeral one is I

explanation.surface: Once a passenger has climbed aboard, the carriage drives off.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light horse-drawn vehicle for one or two people, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Some point one disputed, monotonously uttered

indicators.note: some of the words, a run of letters inside them, gives the answer

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of 'point', all of 'one' and the start of 'disputed'

explanation.surface: A contested point raised in a droning voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite in a chanting, unvarying pitch, as in a church service.

clue.text: Was police chief humming really badly?

parts.note: ran, as in was chief of, headed, the police department
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detective police

explanation.surface: Was the senior officer singing off key?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks like singing with closed lips; it is British slang for smelling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food, especially fat or butter, gives off a foul stale smell.

clue.text: People tending park crushed long piece of wood

parts.note: ground means crushed, as coffee beans are
a staff is a long stick or pole

explanation.surface: Park keepers flattened a wooden pole.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'park' is also slang for a sports ground, such as a football or cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground staff are the workers who maintain a sports field and its surroundings.

clue.text: Side having tail dismissed — reason for break in cricket

indicators.note: the tail, the last letter, is removed; dismissed is also cricket's word for out

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket team loses its lower-order batsmen just before the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the 'tail' is the weak last batsmen; here it is just the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket matches in England pause for an afternoon interval named after the drink taken then.

clue.text: Broken promise for person on half pay?

indicators.note: a broken word is smashed apart and its letters rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A broken pledge leaves someone on reduced wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-professional is paid only partly for a sport or job, so cryptically someone on half pay; the question mark flags the play.

clue.text: Seed used in recipe, appearing repeatedly? Just so

indicators.note: the letters are used within the phrase, run across the word gap

parts.note: the answer spans the last two letters of 'recipe' and the first of 'appearing'

explanation.surface: An ingredient keeps turning up in a cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' is apt: the same three letters also sit inside 'appearing' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is the round seed of a climbing legume, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Greek character not liking Italian wine

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter X
anti means against, opposed to

explanation.surface: A Greek man doesn't care for wine from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine produced in Tuscany, central Italy.

clue.text: Gambling device from casino near Med band itself extracted

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from within the run of words, ignoring the spaces

parts.note: the answer starts at the end of 'casino' and runs through 'near Med band' into 'itself'

explanation.surface: A slot machine is taken from a Mediterranean casino by a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, worked by a lever and notorious for taking players' money.
